title: Machine-checked proof of the unique-zero conjecture (OEIS A084030)
description:
Machine-checked proof of the conjecture recorded on OEIS A084029 and A084030. Canonical statements (verbatim): A084029 %N - "Triangle read by rows: n-th row contains the first n n-digit multiples of n with digit sum n. If there are fewer than n such numbers, the rest of the row is filled with 0's." A084030 %N - "Main diagonal of triangle A084029." Both entries (Amarnath Murthy, May 24 2003; extended by David Wasserman, Dec 09 2004) carry the same UNSIGNED comment: "Conjecture: Only one term is zero."

NEW IN v6: the diagonal term itself is now a formalized object. Module A084030Val defines a084030_val n = sInf(Tdiag n), the n-th smallest witness of row n (sInf of the empty set is 0, matching exactly the OEIS zero-padding convention), and theorem a084030_val_zero_iff proves a(n) = 0 iff n = 2 for every n >= 1 - the conjecture carried on the object itself, not only on row cardinalities. Sixteen kernel-certified anchors prove the listed values a(1)=1, a(2)=0, a(3)=120, a(4)=2020, a(5)=10400, a(6)=100140, a(7)=1001203, a(8)=10001312, a(9)=100000080, a(10)=1000000900, a(11)=10000010108, a(12)=100000000524, a(13)=1000000002235, a(14)=10000000002650, a(15)=100000000000950, a(16)=1000000000003408, each with the complete list of smaller witnesses decided inside the kernel. TRUST BASE REDUCED: the previously disclosed native_decide certificate on the 128-row witness table is gone - table029_ok_all is now proved by decide +kernel certificates split per sub-range (modules Scratch029_cert_*); every exported theorem prints axioms = [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

theorem A084030 proves, for every n >= 3, that the witness set of row n has at least n elements - the row is full, no zero-padding, so the diagonal term is nonzero (a084030_val_pos). theorem A084030_zero_unique certifies (witnesses 2).card = 1 - the singleton {20} - giving the unique zero a(2) = 0; theorem A084030_one gives a(1) = 1. A companion corollary theorem A084033 covers the quotient triangle T(n,k) = A084029(n,k)/n (no conjecture on that entry): for n >= 3 every quotient row has >= n integer terms, all nonzero. The heavy lifting is the A084029 row-existence theorem (two-block construction for n >= 131, certified witness table for 3 <= n <= 130), itself built on the published A077754 Murthy engine.

Prior art: none found - to our knowledge as of 2026-11-04 this is the first written proof and first machine-checked formalization (search corpus and date evidenced in VERIFICATIONS/anteriorite.md).

Certification: Lean 4 + mathlib v4.35.0 (pinned lean-toolchain + lakefile.toml + lake-manifest.json inside lean-artifact/, fourteen modules). Rebuild from the archive on a clean machine (elan + network required): cd lean-artifact && lake exe cache get && lake build - exits 0 with zero sorry and zero admit. Axiom bases (#print axioms, VERIFICATIONS/axioms.txt): every exported theorem carries the three standard axioms only - no native_decide, no ofReduceBool, no sorryAx anywhere in the delivered chain. Fidelity of the formalized statements to the raw OEIS text was audited blind by an external oracle (verdict VRAI); the hardened object-level audit (VERIFICATIONS/D2PLUS/, adversarial referee verdict SOLIDE) confirmed a084030_val is exactly the OEIS diagonal term; the exchanges are archived under VERIFICATIONS/.

Contents: the note in Markdown/TeX/PDF, lean-artifact/ (14 modules + pinned build files), VERIFICATIONS/ (OEIS snapshots, oracle audits, anteriority audit, D2PLUS/ hardening audit, MANIFEST.sha256, rebuild log), ANNONCES.md, metadata.json, NOTICE.txt.
